description: The plot illustrates how accuracy (ACC) varies with co-occurrence number for six methods (Base, FT, IKE, MEND, MEMIT, and ROME). The x-axis is labeled “Co-occurrence Number” and uses a logarithmic scale, spanning from about 0 to a few thousand, with major ticks shown at 0, 10¹, 10², and 10³. The y-axis is labeled “ACC (%)” on a linear scale, ranging roughly from the high 20s to just under 60, with labeled ticks at 30, 40, 45, 50, and 55. The Base series is a black solid line with circular markers, increasing from about 28 at the leftmost point to about 31 near the middle and ending around 31 at the rightmost point. FT is a blue solid line with downward-triangle markers, rising from about 32 at the leftmost point to about 35–36 at the next point and ending around 38 at the rightmost point. IKE is a red solid line with upward-triangle markers, increasing from about 33 at the leftmost point to about 37–38 at the next point and ending around 41 at the rightmost point. MEND is a brown solid line with diamond markers, rising from about 36–37 at the leftmost point to about 41 at the next point and ending around 45–46 at the rightmost point. MEMIT is a purple solid line with pentagon markers, increasing from about 36 at the leftmost point to about 43 at the next point and ending around 46–47 at the rightmost point. ROME is a green solid line with square markers, rising from about 44 at the leftmost point to about 49 at the next point, reaching about 56 near the middle-right, and ending around 58–59 at the rightmost point.
